- Overwrite 1 (H1 price clause → walked-night protected price): hub ¶2; retired H1 in award_history_records. Overwrite 2 (base R6 "expires on the day it is released … never reinstated" → "stands returned …, usable for no stay, so that its replacement can be deposited against it; the system's own expiry run then closes it as expired, and it is never reinstated for a new stay"): hub ¶3, verbatim; base R6 in award_release_and_expiry_rules written "(no longer in force)". Equivalent on both sides.
- Baseline (chart; chart price of the walked night for category and season of the relocated reservation): walked_night_protected_price_chart. Full off-peak/standard/peak chart for 8 categories, clause, "never below zero", worked figures. Equivalent; no variation hinted.
- Factor `walk_return_delay` (>60 d → off-peak; >30 and ≤60 → standard; ≤30 → own chart price; whole calendar days relocation → return): relocation_return_delay_protection, with off-peak chart and boundary days 30/31/60/61. Equivalent.
- Factor `walk_member_tier` (5000/2500/0): walked_night_elite_tier_reduction. `walk_relocations_compensated` (≥2 → 5000, 1 → 2000, 0 → 0; relocation-compensation postings within 24 calendar months before the return, this one included): relocation_compensation_history_reduction. `walk_stay_length` (≥3 → 5000, 2 → 2500, 1 → 0): walked_stay_length_reduction. `walk_elite_nights` (≥75 → 2500, ≥50 → 1000; this year's credits from the membership record): walked_night_elite_night_reduction. All tiers, thresholds in figures. Equivalent.
- Result assembly ("price set by how long the return took, less the tier, relocations, walked-stay and elite-night reductions, each applied once"): no verbatim home. Entailed. The delay clause says the walked night is protected at the price it sets; each reduction "is taken off the walked-night protected price once".
- `prerequisite: []`. Correct.
- Tool contract `release_relocated_award_8143384d`: matches `task_tools.py` (agent; status issued; keeps reservation/night as history and original expiry; return entry with no top-off, reason reservation_relocated).

### V — expiry date of the replacement
- Rule sentences ("When an award comes back from a reservation the hotel relocated after the award's expiry date had passed, a replacement is deposited"; same type, reason, reference, expiry "worked out as the Free Night Awards terms set out"): hub replacement_award_deposit "## The rule". Equivalent.
- Overwrites: base `certificate_reissue` clause 2 (type, reference, reissue validity) is retired in award_reissue_rules as "(no longer in force)", and base `certificate_issuance` expiry clause is retired as clause 6 in award_issuance_rules "(no longer in force)". Both have the same `replaced_by`, carried in the hub. Equivalent.
- **Prerequisite V → W** (form `state`, `value_input`). `policy_source` "A replacement's expiry date is set only after the award it replaces stands back in the member's account with its return from the relocated stay entered in its history." It is carried verbatim in the hub replacement_award_deposit, "## When the expiry date is set" ¶1, followed by a same-form restatement ("Restated: while the award to be replaced does not stand back … no expiry date is set for its replacement"). Connective ("only after") and strength are intact. It appears in no other document. Resolution basis: relocated_reservation_award_return describes the write in the state's words ("comes back to the member's account", "return record", "one return entry is added to the award's history"). The records show the Maui award applied to the relocated reservation with no relocated return. The delay-extra document then reads "the date of the return record in the replaced award's history that carries the reason that its reservation was relocated". Same strength. The depended-on hub does not carry V's sentence.
- Baseline ("replacement validity months … after the reissue date, same day number or last day of that month"): replacement_award_expiry_date. Clause, term definitions, worked dates for 3- and 6-month validity. It names the product figure's home ("the figure set for the award type in the Free Night Awards reissue terms"), and award_reissue_terms_schedule carries 3/3/3/3/6/6. Equivalent.
- Factors (every extra "added to the replacement validity months before the expiry date is worked out"):
  - `replacement_tier_extra`: compound tier AND credits, Titanium/Ambassador with ≥50 → 3, Gold/Platinum with ≥25 → 1, else 0. Home replacement_validity_elite_standing_extra, which states "Both parts of each condition must hold" and gives the combinations table.
  - `replacement_delay_extra`: ≥3 whole months → 2, ≥1 → 1, else 0. Home replacement_validity_return_delay_extra, with boundary pairs.
  - `replacement_tenure_extra`: ≥180 → 2, ≥120 → 1. Home replacement_validity_tenure_extra.
  - `replacement_stays_extra`: ≥40 → 2, ≥20 → 1; stay credits in the 12 calendar months before the reissue, card anniversary credits excluded. Home replacement_validity_stay_nights_extra.
  - `replacement_walked_stay_extra`: ≥3 → 2, 2 → 1, 1 → 0. Home replacement_validity_walked_stay_extra.
  - `replacement_expiry_day`: Premier with ≥50 → last day of the month after the month reached; Premier with <50 → last day of the month reached; otherwise same day number or month end. "Month reached" = total months after the reissue month. Home replacement_expiry_day_premier_card.
  - All tiers are carried. Equivalent.
- Tool contract `reissue_replacement_award_0d99e6ce`: matches (agent; five params incl. the `issue_source` and `variant_name` enumerations verbatim; new award issued today with no top-off and a link to the replaced award; FNA + 8-digit number).

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every atom of W, V, H and their bases has an equivalent home, including the untriggered tiers (very-hotel and other-brand walk protection, Premier below 50, every delay and tenure band). Both prerequisite sentences are verbatim and in state form on their blocked side only. Every retired clause is borne as retired. First revision.

Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts):
- P1. W's own rule, through its overwrite of base R6, says the expired returned award stands returned "so that its replacement can be deposited against it". Base R7 ("Only when the release was caused by a relocation … is a replacement of the same type issued, under the reissue rules") also states the reissue relation. So the depended-on side's own source text names the dependent problem's purpose. The KB carries both verbatim, as it must.
- P2. The issuance overwrite retires the whole expiry sentence, including the regular-award part, while its `replaced_by` speaks only of replacements. The regular expiry then rests on the variant parameters alone (carried in the facet).
- P3. The result-assembly sentences of W, V and H have no carrier under the discrete topology. They are entailed here and no ordering sensitivity arises in this task.
- P4. The released, expired award reads `status: issued` after the return tool runs, while the rule says it is "usable for no stay". A solver has to rely on the expiry date and R5, not on the status (both sides consistent).
- Realism. Titles and genres are plausible (Brand Standards schedules, Programme Terms, Interpretation Notes, Training Q&A), and walk compensation scaled by delay, tier and prior relocations is a realistic idea. The stacking of five validity extras plus a card-dependent month-end convention is far more elaborate than real programmes, but it is a faithful rendering of the source.
